novel_features.name: Served-meal history
novel_features.description: See every meal actually served to you over time, with date, venue, price, and dietary level.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local join across synced deliveries, orders, pieces, and menus over weeks or months; the web app shows one delivery at a time and never aggregates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs a longitudinal view of what a person has eaten, not just the current delivery.

novel_features.name: Preference-vs-served drift
novel_features.description: Flag served meals that violate your stated dislikes or dietary restrictions, or miss your likes.
novel_features.rationale: Mechanical set-membership join of your profile preferences against served meal items in the local store; no such conformance view exists in the product.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to audit whether auto-selection is actually honoring dietary preferences over time.

novel_features.name: Auto-selection explainer
novel_features.description: Explain why a delivery's meal was auto-selected by ranking candidate items and their scores.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the auto-selection scores with menu items and your preferences locally; the web app hides the scoring entirely.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this to explain a single day's auto-selected meal; use preference-drift for aggregate conformance.

novel_features.name: Spend trend over time
novel_features.description: Bucket lunch spend into per-week or per-month totals with CSV export.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates delivery receipts into billing-period buckets in the local store; the product has no cross-period spend view or export.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when finance needs a time series of lunch cost, not a single delivery receipt.

novel_features.name: Allowance utilization
novel_features.description: Show granted-vs-consumed allowance utilization per club, including multi-club comparison.
novel_features.rationale: Joins club allowance settings against delivery receipts locally; enables cross-team comparison the product never surfaces.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to see which teams are over- or under-using their lunch budget.

novel_features.name: Week-ahead digest
novel_features.description: One agent-shaped line per upcoming day: date, venue, auto-selected item, price, allowance headroom.
novel_features.rationale: Joins in-progress and future deliveries with menus into a compact briefing; agent-native output the SPA does not offer.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this for a quick 'what's coming this week' summary an agent can read in one shot.

novel_features.name: Venue rotation
novel_features.description: Rank venues by how often they've served you and how recently.
novel_features.rationale: Computes served-frequency and days-since-last-seen from the local store; distinct from the single-venue usage endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to spot venue fatigue or under-used favorites across the whole synced window.

narrative.headline: A CLI and MCP server for your Forkable office-lunch program, with a local database and history, spend, and preference queries the web app cannot answer, plus commands to set, confirm, and skip meal orders (dry-run by default; --confirm to apply).
narrative.value_prop: Forkable exposes no public API. This CLI reverse-engineers the my-account app's GraphQL surface into a Go binary with clean read commands and agent-native output. On top of the raw reads it adds longitudinal views the product never shows — served-meal history, preference-vs-served drift, spend trends, allowance utilization, venue rotation, and a week-ahead digest — all fetched live from Forkable. It also exposes the my-account app's own meal-management mutations as meal set, meal set-all, meal confirm, meal skip, and reorder; these are dry-run by default and only place, confirm, or skip real orders when you pass --confirm.
narrative.auth_narrative: Forkable authenticates with a browser session cookie plus a per-request CSRF token fetched from /api/v2/csrf_token. Log in to forkable.com in Chrome, then run 'forkable-pp-cli auth login --chrome' to import your session. There is no API key.

quickstart.comment: Verify the binary, config, and auth wiring before hitting the API.
Import your logged-in Forkable session from Chrome (no API key exists).
Confirm auth works by fetching your profile and preferences.
See what you've actually eaten over the last quarter (fetched live).
Export per-month lunch spend for finance.

troubleshoots.fix: Your session expired; re-run 'forkable-pp-cli auth login --chrome' after logging in to forkable.com in Chrome.

troubleshoots.symptom: A GraphQL query with placeholder ids returns empty
troubleshoots.fix: menus/meal-scores/venue-usage need real ids: get them from 'deliveries list' (availableMenuIds) and 'clubs list', then pass a custom --query.

troubleshoots.symptom: History or trend commands show nothing
troubleshoots.fix: These fetch live from Forkable; make sure 'account --json' works first, then widen the window with --since 180d.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or script needs to query a Forkable office-lunch program from the terminal: what meals were served, how much was spent, which venues rotate, and whether served meals match stated dietary preferences. It is the only programmatic surface for Forkable and the only way to get longitudinal history the web app does not aggregate. It can also set, confirm, and skip upcoming meal deliveries on the user's behalf — those commands are dry-run by default and require --confirm to apply. All commands fetch live from Forkable (no local sync step).
anti_triggers: Do not place, change, or cancel meal orders without explicit user intent — the meal set, meal set-all, meal confirm, meal skip, and reorder commands mutate the real account and require --confirm; run them dry-run first and confirm the printed mutation before adding --confirm.
Do not use this CLI to add or remove club members or manage billing — use the Forkable web app.
Do not use this CLI for real-time delivery tracking notifications — those come via Forkable's email/Slack/SMS.
